title: Properties of Light
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Properties of Light Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_code: Grade 8, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Light travels in straight lines; reflection and refraction; the colors of the visible spectrum; how we see objects. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy): how light travels, reflection, refraction, color and the spectrum and how we see. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines at about 300 000 km per second. Opaque objects block light and make shadows; transparent materials let light through; translucent materials let some through. We see objects when light from them enters our eyes.

A mirror reflects light: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Light bends (refracts) when it passes from one material to another, such as from air into water. A prism splits white light into the spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

Example

A ray hits a mirror at 40°. What is the angle of reflection?

They are equal.

Answer: 40°

Example

Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

Light changes speed.

Answer: refraction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we see because light leaves our eyes.
  • Thinking white light is one color.
  • Thinking a red shirt absorbs red light.

faq.q: Why does a red apple look red?
faq.a: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colors.
Raindrops refract and split sunlight into its colors.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a candle flame, a flash of lightning, a glowing computer screen or the Moon?
items.e: The Moon does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Light travels about 300,000 km every second. How far does it travel in 2 seconds?
Is a stone wall transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A stone wall lets no light through and makes a dark shadow.

items.q: Is wood transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Wood lets no light through and makes a dark shadow.

items.q: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth. If a planet were 3 times as far from the Sun as Earth, about how long would sunlight take to reach it?
items.e: Twice as far takes twice as long, and so on.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a candle flame, a flash of lightning, a lit bulb or a sheet of white paper?
items.e: A sheet of white paper does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Which of these is a light source: a campfire, a high-visibility jacket, a mirror or the Moon?
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: Is plastic wrap transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Cling film lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Is a lampshade transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: A lampshade lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a candle flame, a firefly, a glowing computer screen or the planet Venus?
items.e: The planet Venus does not make its own light; it reflects light.

items.q: Is clean water transparent, translucent or opaque?
items.e: Clean water lets almost all light through, so you can see clearly through it.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a light source: a campfire, a mirror, a star or the Sun?

items.q: A green hat is lit only by blue light. What color does it look?
items.e: Objects reflect their own color and absorb the others. If their color is not in the light, they look black.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 20°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Law of reflection: angle of incidence = angle of reflection (both measured from the normal).

items.q: A green hat is lit only by green light. What color does it look?
items.e: Objects reflect their own color and absorb the others. If their color is not in the light, they look black.

items.q: A ray of light makes an angle of 40° with the surface of a mirror. What is the angle of incidence (measured from the normal)?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so 90° − 40° = 50°.

items.q: Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
c: It is not changed from left to right.
It is real (it can be caught on a screen).
It is laterally inverted (left and right are swapped).
items.e: A plane mirror image is upright, the same size, laterally inverted, virtual and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: A red T-shirt is lit only by red light. What color does it look?
items.e: Objects reflect their own color and absorb the others. If their color is not in the light, they look black.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the mirror surface is 40°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angles are measured from the normal: 90° − 40° = 50°, and i = r.

items.q: Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
c: It is larger than the object.
It is not changed from left to right.
It is the same size as the object.
It is real (it can be caught on a screen).
items.e: A plane mirror image is upright, the same size, laterally inverted, virtual and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: The angle of reflection at a plane mirror is 55°. What is the angle between the reflected ray and the mirror surface?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so the angle is 90° − 55° = 35°.

items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so 90° − 10° = 80°.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of refraction.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into water at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: You can read a book from any angle under a lamp. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of diffuse reflection.

items.q: You can see your face in a still pond. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of regular reflection.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A prism splits white light into seven colors. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of dispersion.

items.q: What is the law of reflection?
c: the reflected ray always goes back the same way
angle of incidence = angle of reflection
items.e: For plane mirrors.

items.q: What is white light made of?
c: all the colors of the spectrum mixed together
items.e: A prism separates them.

items.q: A smooth, polished metal tray shows a clear image. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of regular reflection.

items.q: What does the lens in the eye do?
items.e: Like a camera lens.

items.q: A ray of light leaves a glass block into air at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A ray of light goes from air into a glass block at an angle. What happens or why?
c: It bends away from the normal.
It goes straight on without bending.
Light refracts as it leaves the water.
items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through raindrops. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of dispersion.

items.q: A coin at the bottom of a cup of water looks higher than it is. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of refraction.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal (at 90° to the surface). What happens or why?
c: Different colors refract by different amounts.
It bends away from the normal.
It goes straight on without bending.
items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A ray of light passes from water into air at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: How is light different from sound?
c: Light can travel through a vacuum; sound cannot.
items.e: Different waves.

items.q: A ray of light comes out of a glass block into air at an angle. What happens or why?
c: Light refracts as it leaves the water.
It bends away from the normal.
It goes straight on without bending.
Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water.
items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent. Which effect of light explains this?
items.e: This is an example of refraction.

items.q: Vincent drew this diagram to explain how we see the tree. Is it correct?
c: The second arrow points the wrong way: light goes into the eye, not out of it.
